subject: Copywriting
title: Trade Signs and Symbols
description: A 60-second lesson on Trade Signs and Symbols.

hook.text: Most people in medieval Europe couldn't read. Shops used symbols instead: a boot for cobblers, grapes for wine.

buildup.text: These signs transcended language. A traveler from any country could find a blacksmith by the anvil sign.

discovery.text: The barber pole—red and white stripes—dates to when barbers also did surgery. The red meant blood.

twist.text: Pawnbrokers' three gold balls, pharmacies' green cross—these visual logos predate corporate branding.

climax.text: Modern logos are just trade signs evolved. Nike's swoosh works the same way a medieval boot sign did.

punchline.text: Before logos, there were boots and barber poles. Same idea.

quiz.question: Why did medieval shops use symbols instead of words?
